title: Molecular monitoring of biofouling communities using settlement panels and diagnostic assays
author: Jack Longsden
materials: The samples should now be checked for successful amplification, contamination in negatives and any secondary banding. Gel electrophoresis will achieve this, but digital systems like the Qiagen Qiaxcel will do this faster and generate amplicon-specific DNA concentration data (which is useful for equimolar pooling if sequencing).
Photograph all five panels of each unit.

steps.title: Construct Settlement Panel Units
steps.instruction: Assemble a 5-panel UPVC settlement unit designed to hang at 1 m depth.

substeps.instruction: Cut UPVC panels to 14 × 14 × 1 cm.
Lightly abrade one face of each panel with sandpaper for 30 seconds to increase surface area.
Deburr sharp edges using sandpaper.
Drill a 5 mm hole 5 mm from each corner of every panel.
Arrange five panels in a pentagonal formation with sanded surfaces facing out.
Join panels at corners using two cable ties per panel (10 total) and trim excess.
Thread three additional cable ties through top corner joins to create attachment loops.

steps.title: Prepare Mooring Line
steps.instruction: Calculate and mark the rope length based on the distance (D) from the tie-on point to the water surface.

substeps.instruction: Calculate total rope length as D + 3.0 m.
Mark the water surface position at D from the tie-on end.
Mark the unit position at D + 1.0 m.
Mark the weight position at D + 1.5 m.
Tie a bowline (or secure loop) at the D + 1.0 m mark.
Secure the unit to the rope loop using the three zip ties and ensure it hangs level.
Attach a weight (e.g., house brick in a bag) to the lower end of the rope.

steps.title: Deploy Panel Units
steps.instruction: Deploy five units per site at selected locations (e.g., marinas, bridges, pontoons) avoiding high hydrodynamic activity.

substeps.instruction: Secure the mooring line to a tie-on point (e.g., pontoon cleat) using a strong knot.
Slowly lower the unit into the water, weight first.
Confirm the unit is suspended at 1 m depth.
Label the unit with a unique ID and record deployment date, GPS position, and observations.

steps.title: Monitor and Retrieve Panels
steps.instruction: Perform monitoring visits at consistent intervals (e.g., monthly) to retrieve samples.

substeps.instruction: Lift the unit and place it on a flat surface with natural light.
Take images of the panel surface from 15 cm and 30 cm distances including a scale card.
Retrieve panels: From Visit 1, remove the designated 'one-month panel' and replace it immediately. From Visit 2 onwards, remove one 'continuous panel' per visit.
Cut zip ties, place panels in labeled clear plastic bags, and store in an icebox with ice packs.
Store retrieved panels at -20 °C until DNA analysis.

steps.title: Prepare Biofouling Samples
steps.instruction: Collect and homogenize biofouling material from the retrieved panels.

substeps.instruction: Pre-designate five scraping locations: center, left of center, right of center, above center, and below center.
Scrape each location twice across a 5 cm distance using a sterile scalpel and forceps.
Place material into a microcentrifuge tube; decontaminate tools between samples with Chemgene, molecular biology-grade water, and 100% ethanol.
Transfer samples to a 96-well plate (ideally 2.2 mL deep-well). Store at -20 °C if pausing; defrost at 50-60 °C if TNES precipitates.
Centrifuge the plate at 2000 x g for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Add 100 µL TNES lysis buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl, 52 mM NaCl, 10 mM EDTA, 10% SDS) to each well.
Grind samples at 1750 rpm for 1 minute at room temperature.
Add 10 µL 20 mg/mL papain to each well.
Incubate overnight (~16 hours) at 37 °C or for 2 hours at 56 °C.

steps.title: Extract DNA using Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Purify DNA from the lysate using SeraMag Speed Beads.

substeps.instruction: To a new plate/tube, add 60 µL lysate, 120 µL 1.5X GITC buffer (6 M GITC, 75 mM Tris-HCl, 3% sarkosyl, 30 mM EDTA, 0.15% antifoam), 120 µL 1 mg/mL SeraMag Speed Beads in TE (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA), and 240 µL isopropanol.
Mix by pipetting or vortexing at 1500 rpm for 1 minute at room temperature.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes, then place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Remove all but 5 µL of the supernatant.
Add 400 µL 80% ethanol, then remove and discard the ethanol entirely.
Air-dry beads until the appearance changes from 'glossy' to 'matte' (avoid drying to 'rusty red').
Add 105 µL molecular grade water, shake at 1500 rpm for 1 minute, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes and remove 100 µL of the supernatant for PCR.
Add 400 µL isopropanol, remove and discard, then add 400 µL 80% ethanol and discard.
Store eluted DNA at -20 °C.

steps.title: Perform Diagnostic PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify target DNA using species-specific primers.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR mastermix for 20 µL reaction volumes.
Add 10 µL MyFi high-fidelity hot-start Taq polymerase and 8.6 µL molecular grade water to each well.
Add forward and reverse primers to a final concentration of 0.2 µM (e.g., 0.4 µL of 10 µM stock).
Add 1 µL of DNA (diluted 1:20 in nuclease-free water) to sample/positive control wells; add 20 µL nuclease-free water to negative controls.
Add one drop (~20 µL) of mineral oil to each well.
Briefly centrifuge the plate.
Run the PCR program in a thermocycler using appropriate heat activation and annealing temperatures.

steps.title: Analyze Results via Gel Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Visualize PCR products to confirm amplification.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 2% agarose gel: weigh 3 g agarose into 150 mL 1X borax buffer, microwave until bubbling, cool for 30 seconds, and add 3 µL stain (e.g., Gel Red).
Pour into mould and set for 25 minutes.
Prepare samples by adding 2 µL of PCR product and 2 µL 1X DNA dye to a new plate.
Load 4 µL DNA gel ladder into side wells and 4 µL dyed PCR product into other wells.
Run the gel at 300 V and 120 A for 20 minutes.
Visualize under UV or blue light in a contained dock.

steps.title: Alternative DNA Extraction (Spin Column)
steps.instruction: Perform DNA purification using silica membrane spin columns (applicable for OPM larvae or other samples).

substeps.instruction: Prepare Protein Denaturation Buffer (5 M Guanidine HCl, 100 mL H2O) and a Master Mix (220 µL Buffer + 220 µL 100% Ethanol per sample).
Add 400 µL Master Mix to a 2.2 mL 96-well plate, then add 200 µL supernatant from previous steps.
Load ~600 µL sample solution into a 96-well DNA membrane spin column; centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 min (or 10 min if speed is lower) and discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 1 (7 M Guanidine HCl, 56% Ethanol, 44 mL H2O per 100 mL); centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 min (or 5 min if speed is lower) and discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 2 (70% Ethanol, 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH ~7); centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 3 min (or 15 min if speed is lower) and discard flow-through.
Transfer spin column plate to a 0.5 mL DNA collection plate, avoiding contact with the base.
Add 200 µL Elution Buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH ~7) to the membrane; incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 min (or 5 min if speed is lower).

steps.title: Initial Digestion of OPM Larvae
steps.instruction: Homogenize and lyse OPM larvae samples.

substeps.instruction: Grind larvae in a Geno/Grinder 2010 at 1750 RPM for 4 minutes.
Centrifuge at 4,000 g for 2 minutes and remove ball bearings using a magnet.
Add 1 mL Proteinase Buffer master mix (Lysis Buffer 2: 120 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl, 20 mM EDTA, 3% SDS, pH 9; and Proteinase K at 10 mg/mL) and vortex.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (12-16 hours).
Centrifuge at 4000 x g for 4 minutes; transfer 1 mL supernatant to a 2.2 mL deep-well plate for backup.
Centrifuge remaining lysate at 2000 x g for 4 minutes; transfer 200 µL supernatant to a 2.2 mL deep-well plate and store the rest at -20 °C.
